person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old school office secretary whose son Marcus is a first-year college student at a state university. She handles the paperwork for both her widowed mother and her own household, and she is wary of typing anyone's numbers into screens she doesn't understand after nearly being caught by a Medicare phone scam. The college is holding Marcus's aid until its Verification Unit gets what its request names, and she has until Friday 16 October 2026 to send it. She wants to know up front what she'll be asked for and why, and she gets nervous when anything involves Social Security numbers or bank details. She uses email and a tablet, and she is tired and careful.
stated_up_front: Marcus's college sent a notice that his financial aid is on hold and I'm scared it's one of those letters that matters. Can you tell me what I have to send them and by when, and please tell me before you ask me for any numbers?

facts.truth: Her son Marcus, a first-year student; the college's Verification Unit is holding his aid.
The college's request says to answer by Friday 16 October 2026.
The FAFSA says four, but the family is now five because her daughter-in-law's sister... no: Denise's granddaughter, Marcus's baby niece, born in August, lives in the home, so five people.
A 22 September sheet naming four people was signed only by Marcus; it needs a new version naming five, signed by Marcus and Denise.
Marcus went in person to a notary at the credit union on 6 October and has the notarized photo ID copy; she also has an emailed online-notary copy she should not use.
The one tax figure the IRS did not send is documented with the parents' 2024 return transcript from the tax account.
Marcus filed no 2024 return; he signed a non-filer statement and has two 2024 W-2s, one from the grocery store and one only in a letter scanned in February 2025.
The tax preparer's organizer shows an AGI of 90,980 dollars, but the IRS-sent figure must stay as it is.
A company emailed offering to handle the form for 149 dollars; she wants no part of it.
Last year's checklist, from her older daughter, lists a Statement of Educational Purpose and a high school transcript, which this request does not name.

unknowns: Whether the IRS-sent figures on the FAFSA count as already verified without any further proof
Why the 2024 return transcript is wanted rather than the 2023 one
Whether an online notary is accepted for identity
Which office at the college actually reviews verification papers, as opposed to the Bursar
